lesson.title: Negative Numbers on a Number Line
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you connected negative numbers to real situations. Today: place them on a number line!

A number line extends in both directions from zero: positive numbers to the right, negative numbers to the left. The farther left a number is, the smaller its value — so -8 is less than -3, even though 8 is a bigger number than 3! Draw a number line from -10 to 10, and place these numbers on it: -7, 3, -2, 8.
You just placed negative numbers on a number line! Tomorrow we'll learn about absolute value: distance from zero.

objectives: Place positive and negative numbers correctly on a number line
Understand that further-left numbers on the line are smaller, correcting a common misconception
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's real-world negative-number examples.
2. Draw a number line together, placing -7, 3, -2, 8.
3. Discuss why -8 is less than -3, correcting the 'bigger number = bigger value' misconception.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's absolute-value lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a real ruler or a taped number line on the floor for the child to physically walk along
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why -8 is less than -3 in their own words
The 'bigger number, smaller value' misconception with negatives is genuinely common at this age — name it explicitly rather than just showing the correct placement
teacherGuide.answerKey: On the number line, -7 is furthest left, then -2, then 3, then 8 furthest right — correctly ordered from least to greatest.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 6 standard 6.NS.6c: finding and positioning integers on a number line, continuing this week's negative-numbers thread.
